page: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture with 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 virtual CPUs running at 2.7 GHz, operating without simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache pool. The configuration includes 768.0 GB of DDR5 system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per core balance. It features a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated GPUs, and includes no local SSD storage, necessitating network-attached storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant multi-threaded throughput across diverse computational tasks. The instance achieved top-tier standing in multi-core stress-ng (304,250.8) and Geekbench multi-core (20,860.0), alongside top-decile scores in Clang software compilation (88,602.0) and ray tracing (122,066.0). Memory throughput is robust, recording 897.11 GB/sec on uncached read-only large blocks and 425.8 GB/sec on uncached writes. Database and web performance are similarly strong, registering 360.85 million Redis SET operations per second and 136.65 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-core metrics sit squarely in the middle 50%, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1,667.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 1,648.5.

Workloads relying on massive thread counts benefit from the full hardware-level access of the bare-metal architecture and the high DDR5 memory bandwidth. However, large-language-model text generation metrics remain lower tier, posting 2.66 tokens/sec on 70B models and 58.82 tokens/sec on 135M models due to the absence of dedicated hardware acceleration. The lack of built-in local disks also requires external storage integration for persistence. The instance fits heavy multi-threaded workloads such as distributed caching, code compilation, container consolidation, large relational or in-memory databases, and high-concurrency web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose instance featuring 192 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture at 2.7 GHz without multithreading. It provides 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, allocating 4.0 GB per core, and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. It has no bundled GPUs and provides no local NVMe storage. Benchmarks place the system in the top tier for multi-core processing, recording 304,250.8 in stress-ng and 20,860.0 in Geekbench, backed by 897.11 GB/sec of uncached read memory bandwidth and 360.85 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-core performance and CPU-based LLM token generation are moderate to weak. The server fits high-concurrency environments, memory caching, software compilation pipelines, and containerized deployments.
